decision.rationale: No single supported, mutation-free, persistent editor-state bridge preserves every native shell owner; CP1 already supplies the complete reversible completion path.

shell_matrix.prototype: ICommandPredictor plug-in inside the existing host
COMP_LINE and COMP_POINT only inside completion
BUFFER and CURSOR only inside a completion widget
commandline state only inside a Fish function or binding
no supported rich completion or editor-state API

shell_matrix.baseline: WSL2 with a supported guest shell
shell_matrix.prototype: delegate to the guest shell; no host grid inference
shell_matrix.local_evidence: WSL2 available with Bash guest evidence

dependency_decisions.name: in-tree-deterministic-matcher
dependency_decisions.boundary: existing local quick-action and palette search

dependency_decisions.name: carapace
dependency_decisions.boundary: never bundle or invoke per keystroke

evidence_dimensions.native_completion_and_prediction: official shell contracts plus CP1 conformance
evidence_dimensions.typing_latency: zero Automexia delta because no runtime surface ships
evidence_dimensions.memory: zero Automexia resident delta because no runtime surface ships
evidence_dimensions.cancellation: generation rejection prototype and benchmark corpus
evidence_dimensions.resize: native shell UI remains owner; CP1 fallback is unchanged
evidence_dimensions.accessibility: native shell UI remains owner; controlled screen-reader evidence is external
evidence_dimensions.disable: CP1 disable and uninstall contracts remain authoritative
evidence_dimensions.privacy: zero shipped delta; no transport, persistence, history read, or grid inference

external_gates: controlled native Zsh and Fish interaction measurements
controlled Windows, Linux, and macOS screen-reader assessment
low-end hardware matcher and shell startup replication
a separately accepted bridge ADR and machine threat contract before P2
